title: Aura of Intelligence for disaster resilience and recovery
text: Start with people. Build capability together. Aura of Intelligence is Luke Nathan Hayes’s proposal for adaptive support throughout life. A personal Aura would help someone reflect, learn, organise chosen records and understand the next useful step. For disaster resilience, that relationship meets a practical community network: trusted information, local knowledge, learning, equipment and people who follow through. The starting place is Minjerribah, North Stradbroke Island, and Redlands. Community discussion, demonstrations and measured trials would shape a path through Queensland and Australia. The ambition is substantial; the public research, document and wiki give interested people a concrete place to begin. [P1] A demanding transition. A constructive bet. Smartphones already bring computing, cameras, microphones and location tools into daily life. An ACCC-commissioned survey found that 94% of Australians aged 14 and older had a personal smartphone in October-November 2024. This is a dated survey finding, rather than a claim about every household today. [R1] Artificial intelligence, or AI, adds ways to explain information and work with records. Superintelligence, or SI, describes possible capability beyond humans across many fields; its arrival is uncertain. Extended reality, or XR, connects digital material with real surroundings or immersive practice. Increasingly capable devices, sensors and robotics make personal agency and practical learning urgent concerns. [R2] Australia has less than six years before Brisbane 2032. The next season of disruption arrives much sooner. Aura proposes a Protopian gambit : a considered bet on improvements people test, compare and revise. Joyful Responsible Abundance joins worthwhile experiences, care for consequences and wider access to useful capability. A fair go includes people whose circumstances make preparation harder. The person remains the starting point The qualified self. A person is understood through their own explanations, values, abilities, relationships and experience. Measurements add observations; reflection gives them meaning. Onboarding records a minimum viable self , the first agreed representation from which a personal digital twin grows. People own their data and digital twins in Aura’s proposed model, with chosen services providing the business proposition. [P2] Meet the personal Aura → Useful before the storm. Useful long afterwards. Music, sport, culture, shared meals and practical work give a resilience network an everyday home. Familiar information points and people become easier to find when circumstances change. During disruption, the proposed service would preserve source meaning, show connection limits and keep requests traceable. Recovery continues through changing needs, memories, rest, work and renewed participation. Paid Try Everything opportunities, voluntary civic stewardship and community-shaped C-Hours offer different ways to contribute. Essential assistance follows people’s needs and actual service arrangements, independently of any contribution record. Where the work stands Available to examine The document, linked research, source archive, design questions, wiki and personal browser-tool foundations. Next to demonstrate A complete journey using sample people, notices, requests, learning tasks, interruptions and restoration. To develop with participants Hosts, protected personal continuity, measured equipment, service agreements, funding and supported trials. Publication of a plan establishes neither an operating emergency service nor an agency partnership. Early interest helps prioritise worthwhile work and develop shared targets and mutually acceptable terms. Explore a first contribution ↗

title: A personal Aura, beginning with you
text: Your explanation gives the record meaning. The qualified self is the person understood through their own account of what matters, what helps and what they have experienced. A pulse reading, location or photograph is an observation. The person’s explanation supplies context: effort, enjoyment, a difficult day, company or a changing need. A digital twin is a versioned representation of selected aspects of a person, place or system. A personal twin develops through chosen records, reflection and later experience. The person reviews an AI interpretation, corrects it or rejects it. A richer record earns its usefulness through that continuing relationship. [P2] Onboarding records a minimum viable self. Onboarding is the guided introduction to Aura. It begins with a purpose, such as bringing a household plan together, explaining a support arrangement or exploring a community role. A demonstration with sample material lets someone see the process before supplying personal records. The minimum viable self is the first agreed representation of selected aspects of body, mind and life. Incomplete and uncertain information stays visible. The account grows through use, without requiring a complete life history at the outset. [P2, P3] A practical starting conversation Starting point What it helps explain Present life Chosen name, language, relationships and current circumstances. Meaning and preferences The person’s own words for what matters and how they learn. Body and practical context Relevant abilities, access or equipment needs, with their source. Experience Useful skills, earlier learning and actual credentials. Intentions and boundaries The starting purpose, chosen audiences and agreed uses of records. A person’s account, a document, a measurement and an AI interpretation keep their different origins. Optional photographs or body references have an explained purpose. An information enquiry has a much smaller requirement than a developing personal twin. Self-sovereign data, made practical. People own their data and digital twins in Aura’s proposed arrangement. Useful ownership means understandable storage, chosen sharing, correction, usable copies and a route to move between providers. The business earns from services people choose. Selling personal access as the product is contrary to this direction. Level Zero, shortened to L0, names the person’s controlled private environment: their chosen devices, storage and services. A continuity plan examines a lost phone, damaged equipment, forgotten access details and unavailable outside services. The question is what remains retrievable, and who the person has chosen to assist. Aura Matrix Studio already offers editable browser records and exports. Its present browser storage is an early implementation; a protected vault, personal model training and dependable external actions remain development work. A disaster trial would use protection tested for its actual people and records. [P3] A receiving service gets the information relevant to the task, with purpose, recipient and retained copies explained. Privacy and emergency-sharing duties depend on the entity and circumstances; federal and Queensland guidance provide the legal context. [R12, R13] A public doorway stays open. Guest and assisted routes remain part of the proposed public service. Notices and assistance do not depend on a personal Aura, association membership, biometrics or AI-training permission. A shared-device session also needs an understandable ending, including what is cleared from the device. “Light to ultra high definition” describes the depth and usefulness of personal context. Screen resolution, computing location, communications and emergency energy use are separate design choices. Someone seeking one checked notice needs a straightforward experience.

title: Readiness grows in ordinary life
text: Give people a reason to return. A resilience service earns familiarity through ordinary days: finding a local event, learning a useful task, checking a notice or helping maintain shared equipment. Music, sport, culture, environmental care, shared meals and workshops bring people together for enjoyment in its own right. A resident learns where information appears. A host discovers which explanations help. A maintainer notices a dim screen before a major interruption. A person already acquainted with a volunteer coordinator has a familiar starting point when offering help. These relationships give disaster capability an everyday home. [P1] The qualified self develops by taking part. A visitor discovers an interest in explaining things. A retiree enjoys mentoring a learner. A young adult finds that equipment maintenance suits their curiosity. Their Aura would help them reflect on the experience, retain what they recognise as useful and choose a next opportunity. The aim is a fuller relationship with community and intelligence. Someone is welcome to enjoy a meal, attend music or ask a question without turning the encounter into a profile, a contribution target or a training dataset. Enjoyment belongs in the purpose of the service, alongside capability and care. Care for the shared things. Everyday operation exposes unclear messages, inaccessible approaches, damaged equipment and reliance on one enthusiast. A maintenance record gives each issue a next step, a responsible person and a result. Relief practice and time for rest help keep the service sustainable. Paid responsibilities and voluntary contributions follow the actual work. Try Everything and civic stewardship explain the human arrangements; C-Hours explain voluntary recognition and community-shaped reciprocity. Visitors and businesses belong in the picture. A visitor may be unfamiliar with local services. A business has responsibilities to customers, workers and their households. A useful notice preserves the provider’s wording, date and actual operating status: expected reopening is different from confirmed service. A hall, club or business might host an information point, offer a learning opportunity or identify a recurring service problem. Familiarity with a venue helps people find it; activation as a disaster facility comes from the responsible organisation. A first trial would examine a specific benefit, such as fewer repeated enquiries or a clearer handover. [P8] Local tourism and playful teamwork connect with the escape-room research . Their public-facing appeal also creates opportunities to understand a place, practise communication and support paid local skills.

title: Prepare around the life people actually live
text: Turn a broad intention into a useful conversation. Get Ready Queensland introduces understanding local risk, making a plan and preparing an emergency kit. Aura’s proposed contribution is to help someone connect that guidance with their circumstances and organise a manageable next step. Official information retains its source. [R3] A household may have a plan scattered through messages and paper. The first task might be checking contacts, finding the relevant local information or discussing who is usually home. Another household begins with pets, a support arrangement or a business on the property. A named contact becomes more useful when that person has agreed to the role. A provider explains its own continuity arrangements. A remembered possibility stays distinct from a confirmed service. Reminders and printed copies follow the tools actually available; dependable background notifications are further development work for the current personal browser tools. [P3] Respect the expertise people already use. Disability, ageing, care responsibilities and changing health needs bring practical knowledge about equipment, transport, communication and support. Inclusive preparedness begins with the person’s account of that knowledge. Get Ready Queensland’s person-centred emergency preparedness resources provide a relevant foundation. [R7] Someone may prefer plain text, captions, speech, a demonstration or time to discuss a choice. A chosen support person might join part of the conversation. The person reviews the account and decides what is shared. Support needs retain their context, rather than quietly becoming fixed AI assumptions. Children and teenagers take part through suitable age, supervision and safeguarding arrangements. Learning and public assistance remain accessible at the appropriate level. An early trial needs actual support roles and referral routes suited to its participants. Country and local knowledge shape the design. Minjerribah is Quandamooka Country. Local participation begins through actual relationships and the people with authority to speak for particular knowledge. Cultural custodians determine the conditions for use, interpretation, audience, copying and AI processing of their material. [P1, R5] Community knowledge also includes how visitors arrive, who cares for shared places, which services people use and what maintenance really involves. A public source does not automatically grant permission to reconstruct a cultural account in a place twin or personal model. The National Principles for Disaster Recovery recognise community context, connections to Country and community-led decisions. The same respect belongs in preparation. [R8] Illustrative exercise · Sample people and messages Anna discovers an assumption. Anna lives with her teenage son and sometimes supports an older relative. In an exercise, her Aura helps gather earlier plans and prepare questions. A transport interruption reveals that she had treated a possible lift as an agreed arrangement. The useful result is a clearer question for the actual people involved. Anna also asks for a shorter explanation with a route back to the original source. That correction becomes part of how her Aura learns to assist her. The exercise demonstrates a learning opportunity, while real preparedness still depends on the arrangements being made. Continue Anna’s exercise →

title: Keep information and responsibility clear
text: Explain the source without changing its meaning. The Australian Warning System uses three levels: Advice, Watch and Act, and Emergency Warning. The issuing organisation’s message and call to action carry the meaning. An Aura explanation would link back to that source and preserve its instructions, location and timing. [R6] A public display needs the issuer, issue time, last receipt and connection state. A stored record remains identifiable when outside links fail. Historical playback, a practice scenario and a current service update need unmistakably different presentation. This website explains the proposal. For current preparedness and warnings, use Get Ready Queensland and the issuing services it links. No live warning feed is operating on these pages. A request moves through real states. Writing a request is the beginning of a journey. The proposed service would show the state confirmed by the device and receiving organisation, making waiting work visible. A personal explanation also stays separate from the organisation’s accepted record. [P7] Proposed request states State What has happened Saved locally The device holds the request; outside delivery is pending. Delivered The receiving system has recorded delivery. Accepted for review A receiving service has taken responsibility for review. Assigned The responsible service has allocated a next action. Outcome recorded The action and any remaining need are recorded. A resource offer also needs a custodian, condition, availability, suitable operator and return arrangements. A vehicle on a list is useful only within its actual readiness and permissions. Paid work, donated resources and voluntary time keep their different records. Illustrative exercise continued Anna’s message waits for a connection. The sample kiosk loses outside internet. Anna prepares a request about a support service. The device saves it locally and explains that delivery is waiting. After restoration, the receiving desk records delivery, then acceptance for review. The exercise deliberately introduces a duplicate. The team checks whether it creates two jobs, whether corrections reach both copies and whether Anna sees a consistent account. A relief steward also takes over, using the current information edition, equipment state and unresolved work. These are proposed test cases, with sample people and services. No actual request is being submitted or monitored by this website. A supported connection with existing services. Guardian IMS is QIT Plus incident-management software. Redland’s December 2025 Local Disaster Management Plan records its use in coordination and tasking. The project explores a supported Aura connection for public information, request preparation and authorised learning. Council and supplier participation, access and exchange arrangements remain to be developed. [R5, R14, P9] A personal Aura does not confer staff access or an agency role. Issuing notices, accepting requests and allocating resources remain decisions for the responsible organisations. The first useful comparison would follow a complete journey, including failure and restoration. [P8]

title: Recovery continues into a fuller life
text: Reduce the work of starting again. Recovery often involves repeated conversations while people manage damage, care, interrupted work and uncertainty. A personal Aura would help retain the history of an enquiry: its reference, actual reply, next agreed action and unresolved questions. A draft note remains different from an accepted service record. Eligibility and assistance decisions stay with the providing organisation. The proposed benefit is a clearer enquiry and visible follow-up, with chosen information available when the person needs it. Queensland recovery planning and Redland’s Alfred recovery record provide the operating context. [R15, R23] A familiar place, kept on your terms. A memory palace uses a familiar place to organise chosen memories. Photographs, stories, objects, sound and selected spatial records might preserve a home, garden or community space that has changed. A person chooses what to retain, revisit, correct or leave alone. A place twin is a dated representation of a location, with its sources and assumptions. Personal recollections have their own meaning. Private memories do not automatically become part of a shared civic model. Reconstruction also respects the rights and cultural authority attached to the material. [P2] {{image:memory-place}} This is supportive continuity to explore. It establishes neither a treatment nor a promise of memory improvement. The person’s wishes, access requirements and wellbeing guide how the experience develops. Leave room for changing priorities. One person wants help with paperwork; another wants a quiet meal. Someone is ready to reconnect through music, sport, culture or environmental care. Rest and professional support have their own place. A disaster becomes part of a person’s history while their interests and possibilities keep growing. The National Principles for Disaster Recovery recognise different pathways and timeframes, community context and participation. Those principles support a continuing personal relationship that changes with the person. [R8] Try Everything opportunities and chosen civic contribution become relevant when someone wants them. No C-Hour target determines access to recovery assistance or a person’s standing in the community. Carry learning into the next season. A weak handover, an inaccessible message or a service dependent on one worker becomes a practical improvement question. Affected people help decide which changes matter. Records identify the tested conditions and whose work remains unresolved. The aim is adaptive whole-of-life support: useful understanding that survives a changed home, device, service or living arrangement, and helps the person develop the next chapter of life.

title: More ways to learn, work and contribute
text: Try a useful role with support. Try Everything Once proposes supported exploration of different kinds of work, with paid scopes and mentoring. A participant might try information upkeep, equipment care, filming a learning item, facilitation, repair or a supervised practical task. The purpose is to discover interests and capability through doing, then reflect on what the experience means. [P5] Paid work follows its actual employment or service arrangement. Time, supervision, access, expectations and feedback form part of a useful opportunity. A person’s preference or an AI assessment alone does not establish a credential. An operating programme, placements and employers remain development milestones. The wider Mutual Futures proposal also explores ownership, income and greater choice over time, including intermittent retirement. These ideas give workforce development a whole-of-life context; they do not establish current entitlements or a funded roster. Civic stewardship is chosen participation. Civic stewardship means helping care for shared places, information, equipment and relationships. It is voluntary community participation. It may involve a short learning item, accessible communication, maintaining a garden or supporting a host’s agreed task. Someone choosing volunteer work needs a meaningful role, suitable induction, support, relief and a way to raise a problem. Australian guidance on spontaneous volunteers and the National Standards for Volunteer Involvement provide useful references. The actual arrangement also determines employment obligations. [R9, R10, R11] C-Hours recognise verified voluntary human time. Paid tasks retain ordinary financial records. Access to essential information and assistance follows the service and people’s needs. A proposed organising home. ready SET Co-op , fully the ready sustainable employment and training cooperative , is the proposed operating intermediary. Formation, membership, mandate, hosts, staffing and funding remain work to develop with interested people. [P11] The proposed council, team and committee model uses shared records so people understand what is being considered, who has accepted a job and what was decided. AI assistants help prepare research and choices. Near-future XR, personal Auras and robotics belong in the design, while actual roles and authority remain traceable. Understand the law in the context of the task. A useful legal introduction begins with the person, activity and location. Your Relevance helps prepare a research brief from chosen circumstances. The connected P4A Legal RAG and Australian Legal Engine explore retrieval with source tracing. [P10, P12] The Australian Legal Engine’s current evidence includes a historical 2012 collection. Understanding a rule’s origin and effects carried forward is valuable; a current decision also needs current provisions, jurisdiction, amendments and relevant professional interpretation. Historical retrieval is an introduction to questions for review. For a learner, that might mean understanding why a role needs a qualified operator, who controls an asset or what a record is used for. Just-in-time learning explains the next permitted task in language suited to the person, with the relevant procedure and qualified help close at hand.

title: C-Hour: reciprocity that strengthens community
text: Time recognised, without a monetary price. One C-Hour recognises one verified elapsed hour of voluntary human contribution. Communities shape their own incentives: access to a private or community event, a shared tool, equipment or another locally agreed opportunity. The purpose is a stronger social fabric. [P4] C-Hours have no monetary equivalent. They are neither sold nor transferred. Each person’s elapsed time is counted once across linked projects. Paid work, money, machine time and outcomes keep separate records. Essential assistance remains independent of any contribution balance. A person volunteering for an hour at a repair gathering records that hour through the host’s agreed process. A paid tradesperson keeps their ordinary paid-work record. AI processing during the session creates no additional human C-Hours. A successful repair is a valuable outcome with its own record. The community chooses a fair arrangement. A host might offer access to a music evening or shared equipment. Availability, access requirements, upkeep and the terms of the offer are worked out locally. Contribution recognition creates no claim over someone else’s property or automatic place at an event. Communities also consider how people with different abilities, caring commitments and available time participate. The purpose is reciprocity and belonging, with room for rest, rather than a universal score of personal worth. During recovery, helping to organise a gathering may be meaningful for one person. Another needs assistance without contributing. Both remain part of the community. Healthy De-Slop is one possible connection. Healthy De-Slop is a connected proposal for community wellbeing and reflection. Locally developed offerings might include sauna, cold therapy, hot and cold experiences, and other suitable activities. A community could choose access to an agreed offering as one reciprocal opportunity. No facility, clinical service or access agreement is established here. [P13] {{image:de-slop}} The proposal also includes adult hyperbaric oxygen therapy , or HBOT : oxygen treatment under increased pressure. Clinical suitability, assessment and delivery belong with qualified providers. The Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital hyperbaric service provides a clinical reference; its inclusion implies no Aura partnership. [R24] HBOT follows its own clinical pathway. A C-Hour record establishes neither eligibility nor treatment benefit. Sauna and cold exposure also need arrangements appropriate to the person, activity and actual provider. The disaster proposal makes no clinical recovery claim for these experiences.

title: A dependable local doorway
text: Three forms to investigate. A public kiosk complements phones, printed material and human assistance. It gives someone a way into a checked notice, agreed service information or a short learning task. A personal Aura uses its own storage and privacy arrangements. Proposed equipment family Form Purpose to explore Sheltered demonstrator Try complete journeys with people and sample records in a manageable setting. Fixed outdoor installation Investigate actual exposure, approach, readability, security, heat and maintenance at a proposed site. Portable continuity kit Restore an agreed information and communication function when a usual location is unavailable. Drawings and component choices are proposals. A safe, accessible site, maintenance cover and measured equipment performance develop through the relevant owners and qualified people. [P6] Continuity is a complete service question. Solar, batteries, grid power, communications and local computing each have a role to examine. A power label alone gives little evidence about the whole service. Testing records the actual loads, useful functions, environment, restoration process and duration observed. A low-energy state might preserve a smaller agreed service. It needs readable information about what remains available, what is stored and what awaits an outside connection. A site becoming unsafe also needs an agreed alternative route, rather than an assumption that every kiosk stays accessible. {{image:continuity-test}} Luke’s firsthand Cyclone Alfred account is five to nine days without grid power depending on location, including nine days at Myora Caravan Park. This is identified as a personal account. It motivates the question of prolonged continuity without establishing an official area-wide outage measurement. [P1] Keep kinds of evidence separate. The first practical exercise is proposed over two to three days. A computer model may simulate a much longer disruption. Simulated duration, computer runtime, bench measurements and real field endurance are different evidence and are recorded separately. Engineering also examines weather exposure, thermal behaviour, power protection, supported communications, accessibility, repair access, replenishment and replacement. The service only claims the conditions and functions actually demonstrated. Installing the Missing Middle adds a useful future question about local compute, useful heat, backup power and equipment renewal. Its proposed connection would need the same site-specific engineering and service tests.

title: Practise together, then learn from the experience
text: A model people are able to question. A place twin is a dated digital representation built from selected evidence and assumptions. It might show an information point, an approach to a venue or a service relationship for an exercise. Its value depends on what it represents accurately and what remains uncertain. A familiar place also offers a setting for a memory palace. Personal memories retain their chosen audience; a public place model uses material cleared for its purpose. A model’s appearance does not establish that an access route, resource or service is currently available. [P1, P2] Learn the next permitted task. Just-in-time learning brings an explanation close to the task. An authorised relief steward might find the current update procedure, watch a short maintained demonstration, practise a handover and receive feedback. The learning item identifies its equipment, procedure edition and review arrangements. Extended reality, or XR, offers digital information in real surroundings and immersive rehearsal. An ordinary screen, spoken explanation or practical demonstration may suit the task better. The person’s access and learning preferences guide the format. Viewing a recording or completing a simulation does not confer a trade qualification, emergency appointment or authority over a service. Qualified supervision and actual permissions remain part of the work. Enjoyable challenges create room to reflect. Escape Room Team Building explores independent group play, followed by reflection on language, listening, evidence, useful disagreement and repair. The current manuscript is the 30 October 2026 ROUND ONE research and calculation edition . Prices, premises, room counts, technology and operating arrangements remain open. [N2] The disaster connection is an opportunity to explore: engaging shared challenges could help people practise communication, problem-solving and information handover, then test whether learning carries into another setting. Screen or XR scenarios remain possible formats, rather than settled escape-room technology. Recording choices cover all capture channels, with workable opt-out and separate decisions about retention, personal Aura use, research and publication. Design, trades, facilitation, filming, editing and mentoring have paid scopes. C-Hours retain their voluntary, non-monetary purpose. The connected Teacher Training source includes outage, transport, weather, water and communications rehearsal using official sources and human roles. It offers a starting reference for discussion. Playful rehearsal builds familiarity; specialist qualifications and operational authority follow their own processes. [N3] Explore the learning research ↗ Current research PDF ↗ Word edition ↗ Prepare for more capable intelligence. AI, SI, XR and robotics are explicit near-future planning concerns. Each proposed use needs a named task, available capability, chosen information, permitted action and observable result. A richer personal relationship with intelligence helps people question its suggestions and direct the work. A rehearsal becomes useful evidence when people explain what happened, the team records mistakes and the next edition changes in response. The AIDR Managing Exercises Handbook provides a relevant Australian reference. [R21]

title: Connect capability without assuming the outcome
text: Installing the Missing Middle. Installing the Missing Middle proposes distributed community computing, useful recovered heat and a pathway into local ownership. Its 29 October 2026 development plan examines installation, commissioning, maintenance and hardware renewal as an ongoing business and workforce opportunity. [N1] The disaster relationship is an extension to investigate. Local services, place simulations and selected records might be supported across devices, community hubs, regional and remote systems. The plan itself establishes neither disaster deployment nor commissioned sites. Ask what keeps working when conditions change. Practical connections to investigate Capability Resilience question Local computing Which useful functions remain available when outside communications are lost? Recovered heat What assessed demand uses it, and what happens when compute or the heat recipient is unavailable? Uninterruptible power supply, or UPS Which loads are protected, for what measured runtime, with what maintenance and longer-duration arrangements? Equipment renewal How are repair, backup, restoration, training and replacement funded and maintained through each generation? A UPS does not establish indefinite operation. A heat-recovery arrangement retains appropriate alternative cooling and heating responses. Pumps, networking and controls belong in the assessment alongside the computers. Specific installation and engineering arrangements develop around each real site. Keep the work useful through generations. Building, plant and computing equipment have different lifecycles. The proposal examines upgrade capacity, renewal funding and suitable continued use for earlier equipment. A move to another task needs assessment; secondary sale and recycling remain other possible outcomes. Selected installation, commissioning and fault recordings could support maintained equipment records, just-in-time learning and paid mentoring. Recording permissions and qualified trade responsibilities travel with the work. Watching a lesson does not confer a licence. [N1, N3] Shared assets and personal ownership have distinct homes. The proposed federation allows people and organisations to cooperate, with shared assets progressing into agreed local ownership. It does not require a compulsory parent company. Personal Auras and private archives remain personal; participation does not automatically transfer them into a civic twin. Voluntary stewardship keeps its C-Hour record. Paid trades, investment, operating finance and equipment ownership use their respective agreements. A C-Hour creates no monetary balance or shareholding. Expressions of interest help identify local readiness and resources. Physical deployment would follow actual site preparation, engineering, people and agreements. The national scale examples in the plan are planning assumptions, with no funding award or rollout timetable established. Read the development plan PDF ↗ Word edition ↗

title: Make the next step concrete
text: Begin with a complete demonstration. The proposed first demonstration uses sample people, notices, requests and locations. Over two to three practical days, participants try everyday tasks, an information change, interrupted communications, a request handover, relief staffing and restoration. Three sample locations and a portable kit provide a possible test arrangement, rather than selected real sites. [P7] Choose a useful journey. A household enquiry, an accessible notice or a relief worker’s handover. Agree the comparison. Work with participants and relevant practitioners to describe the current process and a worthwhile improvement. Try it under changing conditions. Use sample records, named roles and clear exercise boundaries. Review the complete result. Record understanding, follow-through, errors, effort, access and equipment measurements. Develop the next scope. Interested people shape the resources, service arrangements and evidence for a further trial. A simulated week and two days of practical testing remain different evidence. Field endurance claims follow actual measurements. Use the lessons already available. The 2020 Royal Commission into National Natural Disaster Arrangements supplies a national review context. Queensland’s 2025 significant-weather review identifies common-system benefits alongside information-exchange difficulties and duplicated requests during those events. This gives a focused question for Aura: does a clearer enquiry, visible receipt and accountable handover improve the full journey? [R16, R17] Global practice offers comparisons to examine in local context. Wellington’s Community Emergency Hubs foreground community information, skills and resources. Shoalhaven’s information-hub work connects everyday and emergency information after communication disruption. The Sendai Framework brings risk, governance, investment and better recovery into the same view. Inclusion here establishes neither affiliation nor performance equivalence. [R18, R19, R20] Measure benefit without losing the person. Questions for a meaningful comparison Question Evidence Did the person understand? Finding a source, explaining meaning and correcting errors. Did the request follow through? Accurate states, accepted responsibility and unresolved needs. Did learning help? Observed task performance and participant feedback. Did the service continue? Measured availability, information age and restoration. Was the result worthwhile? Personal experience, host effort, costs and willingness to continue. No measured superiority over current services is claimed. Formal human research follows the ethics and governance processes applicable to its design. Any function developed for a medical purpose would have its own clinical evidence and regulatory pathway. The public information and learning service is assessed according to its actual purpose. Expressions of interest are welcome Bring a problem, a possibility or a practical contribution. Early interest creates incentive to prioritise development towards shared targets and mutually acceptable terms. A household might want to try an introduction. A host might offer a demonstration setting. A practitioner might identify a handover worth improving. A tradesperson, carer, artist, driver, researcher or retiree might bring a useful skill. A useful first note describes your interest, the place or people involved, what you would like to explore and a suitable next conversation. Keep household, health and restricted records out of public posts. The public repository provides a visible route for questions and early interest. This website has no submission form and sends no personal details. Open the project discussion space ↗ Resource the stage people choose. A demonstration, an outdoor installation and a continuing service have different costs and responsibilities. Budgets develop around the actual scope: people, qualified input, premises, devices, connections, maintenance, repairs, replacement and support. The Disaster Ready Fund is one reference for funding research, with eligibility and application routes checked for a specific proposal. No award or entitlement is assumed. Paid work and procurement retain ordinary financial arrangements; C-Hour reciprocity remains separate. [R22] Luke initiates and drives the project. Actual technical, cultural, site, receiving-service and statutory decisions remain with the relevant people and processes. The wiki records the choices and evidence so the next step is reviewable. [P11]

title: An independent proposal, open to useful participation
text: About Aura of Intelligence Luke Nathan Hayes is developing Aura of Intelligence as a personal AI operating system and adaptive whole-of-life support direction. The disaster proposal brings qualified self development, self-sovereign records and practical learning into a dependable community-service ambition. GAJRA Earth, the Global Association for Joyful Responsible Abundance on Earth , supplies a values starting point. The work is open to local interpretation, disagreement and improvement. Public information and essential assistance remain independent of pledges or association enrolment. [P1] This is Luke’s independent proposal. Organisations named as sources retain their own responsibilities. References to Council, QIT Plus, public agencies, hospitals, the Olympics or other projects establish no partnership, appointment, funding or endorsement. What is available, and what comes next. The public document, research repository, wiki, associated source publications and this companion website are available to examine. Aura Matrix Studio supplies current browser-tool foundations. An integrated, protected and dependable disaster service still needs demonstrations, technical work, actual hosts, resources, qualified input and service relationships. The new Missing Middle and escape-room connections broaden practical opportunities to investigate. They do not turn proposals into operating installations or programmes. Using this website These are static reading pages. They contain no account registration, advertising, analytics scripts, personal onboarding form or live assistance inbox. Page search runs in the browser against the site’s reading index. The interest-note builder, where used, keeps text in the current page until you copy or download it; it sends nothing. GitHub Pages serves the site and has its own platform practices. Following an outside link takes you to that provider. For the proposed system’s personal-data model, read self-sovereign data ; those design commitments are separate from a claim that this publication hosts a protected personal Aura. Reading and imagery Pages use responsive text, keyboard navigation, a skip link, semantic headings, image descriptions and reduced-motion support. The full document is also available as PDF, Word and HTML text. Feedback on an access barrier is welcome through the project repository. Illustrations are AI-generated concepts commissioned for this website. They depict imagined scenes and equipment, with captions identifying that status. They are neither photographs of deployed Aura services nor evidence of test results. The image provenance record preserves prompts and asset details. Website edition: 30 October 2026. Foundational document: 27 October 2026. Licence and crawler information explain reuse and discovery.
